subject: Acme SLO/SLA follow-up — latency measurement & reporting
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + question on how you'd like latency measured (post-demo)

Thanks again for the time earlier — great demo and appreciate the clarity on the chat UX you're building. Per our call, I wanted to recap the performance targets you mentioned and ask one targeted question so we can align on SLA language.

Recap from call:
- Product: customer-facing chat with streaming token-by-token UX
- Expected typical response length: ~120-200 tokens (median ~150)
- Targets mentioned: p95 first-token latency ~<=250ms, p95 full completion for 150 tokens ~<=1.5s, sustained throughput target ~50 requests/sec with burst to 200 concurrent streams
- Other requirements: per-route observability, weekly performance report during pilot, monthly reporting in production, and contractual remedies for missed SLOs

Question for you:
When you say "latency" for the SLA, do you want us to measure (A) "edge-to-first-token" and "edge-to-last-token" as platform-side metrics (i.e., excluding client network), or (B) end-to-end as seen by the browser client? Most production SLAs measure platform-side (gateway ingress to token egress) to avoid customer network variability — we can provide recommended wording to make that explicit.

Next steps I propose:
1) We’ll draft the suggested SLO clause (measurement windows, exceptions, reporting cadence, remedies) and share as a short PDF.
2) Dev will validate whether the target concurrency/throughput is supported by the Dedicated pool sizing we discussed.
3) If you confirm measurement preference, we’ll bake that into the SLA draft and the pilot success criteria.

Attaching a short workbook where we modeled p95 vs throughput for a 150-token median response (SLO_calculation.xlsx).

Thanks — if you want to jump on a quick 20-min call to lock measurement definitions, I’m available tomorrow 10-12 PT.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachment: SLO_calculation.xlsx (Excel workbook — sample p50/p95 sims)

From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acme.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + question on how you'd like latency measured (post-demo)

Thanks Marissa — this looks right. Quick answers:  
- We prefer platform-side measurements (option A) for the SLA; we’ll measure client-side separately.  
- For streaming UX, the first-token p95 is the most important SLA for us (friction is very sensitive to initial response).  
- We still want an upper-bound guarantee on completion time for standard responses (e.g., 150 tokens) but understand that token-heavy responses can vary.  

Couple of asks:  
1) Please be explicit about outages/maintenance and DDoS as exclusions.  
2) We’d like weekly pilot reports (CSV is fine) and monthly SLA reporting once in production.  
3) On remedies: Acme typically expects service credits tiered by % of SLA misses in a calendar month — can you provide your standard structure so we can review?  

Tom and I can review the draft SLA. If you can get a preliminary clause over by EOD tomorrow that’d be super helpful.

—
Sarah Lee
Product Lead, Search & Assistant
Sarah.Lee@acme.com | (617) 555-0199

Date: 2026-10-05T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Quick recap + question on how you'd like latency measured (post-demo) — Acme confirms platform-side

Rishi / Dev — Acme confirmed they want platform-side measurement (edge-to-first-token and edge-to-last-token). They also want: weekly pilot CSV reports and monthly SLA reporting in production, and explicit exclusions (maintenance, DDoS).

Can Legal/T&C own a draft SLA clause? Rishi — can you put together a short clause (one page) covering:
- Measurement definitions (first-byte/last-byte, p95), 
- Measurement windows (monthly calendar month for SLA, 30-day rolling for internal ops), 
- Exclusions (Maintenance windows, force majeure, DDoS/third-party network issues, customer misconfiguration), 
- Remedies (service credit tiers), 
- Reporting cadence (weekly pilot, monthly prod), 
- Any additional logging/reporting we need to enable on their account for verification.

Dev — can you validate capacity sizing for a Dedicated pool that supports 50 req/s sustained with bursts up to 200 concurrent streaming connections for 150-token responses? Note: Acme cares about first-token p95 <=250ms.

I’ve attached the modeling workbook and will draft an initial clause for legal to tweak.

—
Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acme.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick recap + question on how you'd like latency measured (post-demo) — capacity notes

Quick notes from infra:  
- Baseline: For 150-token median responses with our optimized runtime and streaming enabled, we can meet first-token p95 <=200ms on a Dedicated pool sized for ~30 concurrent hardware-backed model instances per shard (assumes typical MPT-like 8k context model in 4-bit quant).  
- Throughput: 50 req/s sustained is feasible with autoscale; to handle bursts to 200 concurrent streams without head-of-line blocking we recommend a Dedicated pool with warm standby capacity (configured burst instances) or a short cold-start buffer during ramp.  
- Measurement: we record timestamps at gateway receive, first token emitted, and last token emitted. Our proposed SLA language should define latency as the delta between gateway receive and token emit (we can provide both first-token and end-to-end emission metrics).  
- Concurrency caveat: streaming increases memory (KV cache) per connection. If Acme plans to have many long-lived streams, we should size memory accordingly — the workbook has a simple model.  

Action items for us:
1) I'll produce expected pool sizing numbers and estimated monthly cost for Dedicated with the recommended warm-burst config.
2) We'll expose per-route p95 charts and the CSV output for weekly reporting.

—
Dev Patel
Infra/Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>

Subject: Draft SLA clause (redline candidate) — latency measurement, exclusions & remedies

Hi Sarah / Tom — attaching a short draft SLA clause (attached as draft_sla_redwood_v1.pdf) and pasting the core language below for quick scan. This is intended as a starting point for negotiation; we can walk through line-by-line if helpful.

Core proposed language (summary):
- Measurement definitions: "Latency" shall mean the elapsed time between Redwood gateway receipt of a customer request and Redwood's emission of the relevant token(s) to the customer connection. For streaming interactions, two metrics shall be used: "time-to-first-token" (TTFT) and "time-to-last-token" (TTLT). All latency measurements for the SLA will exclude client-side network transit.
- SLO targets: Redwood will aim to meet TTFT p95 <=250ms and TTLT p95 <=1.5s for responses up to 150 tokens under the Dedicated pool sizing agreed between parties.
- Measurement window & reporting: SLA compliance will be measured on a calendar month basis for contractual remedies. Redwood will provide weekly CSV performance reports during the pilot and monthly SLA reports in production. For operational debugging, Redwood will also maintain a 30-day rolling view of percentile metrics.
- Exclusions: The SLA does not apply to (a) scheduled maintenance (with >=48hr notice), (b) force majeure events, (c) third-party network outages or DDoS events outside Redwood's control, and (d) customer misconfigurations that materially affect performance (e.g., sending extremely long contexts, unsupported streaming patterns).
- Remedies: If Redwood fails to meet the agreed SLO for a calendar month, customer may be eligible for service credits calculated as a percentage of that month's Redwood hosting charges. Service credit tiers will be: 5% credit for single SLO misses up to 3% of requests, 10% credit for monthly misses between 3-10%, and 25% credit for misses >10%. Credits are the sole and exclusive remedy.

Please review and let us know any redlines. We can also add a short verification procedure (logs/CSV samples and a jointly-run test harness) if Acme wants a way to validate measured percentiles during the pilot.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call to walk this through.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachment: draft_sla_redwood_v1.pdf (one-page SLA clause)
